Also in practical sense, I used it for some time, and I didn't actually meet anyone new on the site, only a few people I already am friends with. I wasn't very selective. I think this may be related to the fact that it's forcing me to pick a gender that I'm not.  When I'm out and about in the real world, I find it very easy to meet new people, so I think that the lack of this app working for me is more a failure of the app and the way it works or the culture of how people use it, than it is any reflection on me.  It would be minimal effort for the developers to add at least a gender category for "other", and then allow users to search for that. Review: Unlike other connections apps, Tinder relies entirely on chance. You cannot just send a message to someone unless they happen to have liked your pic too. So if you want to spend a week getting only 30 likes a day, and watching the 5 matches during that week auto disappear, this is the perfect app for you! The service doesn't seem to be terribly popular here so I have my radius set to 40 miles.  When I run out of people, I may switch it to 50 miles.  Suddenly I have a new small influx of people within 10 miles of me.  Incidentally, this running out of people thing seems to be way more frequent since the update to the pay model.  I don't know if they're connected, but it's worth noting.  3) Way too many spammers.  The vast majority of matches result in the same message linking to an external site.  If I found the service useful or had any results at all from it, I might--MIGHT--be willing to pay something for it, but a monthly subscription?  No.  A monthly subscription of $20?  Not no, but HELL no. Uninstalling now.

Need to do more about the sceam/ad accounts. Doesn't seem to update messages very often, sometimes messages arrive a few minutes after they were sent. Summa sumarum, I would recommend the app. I've met some interesting people who've become new friends, so it does fulfill it's purpose.

Users make mistakes, that's a fact. 2) To do the same operation (like/nope) on different screens you have wildly different controls (most annoyingly, the buttons are placed sometimes at the bottom, sometimes at the top) 3) The same gesture in two similar screens performs completely different actions: in one case you like/nope, in the other you scroll through photos.
